body.statement: If \(\binom{R+2}{2}\le\ell+3\), then there is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), contained in the image of legal finite-support parameter points, such that every \(\zeta\) in that subset has a curve in the nonempty fiber \(F_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\) along which \(\beta\) varies. Consequently \(L_{\ell}\le r_{\beta}(\ell)\le U_{\ell}\) and \(r_{\beta}(\ell)/\sqrt{2\ell}\to1\).
body.justification: The lower bound is robust on a legal moment chart rather than resting on one algebraic or nonreal witness.
body.gap: Neither the anchor nor generic dimension counting constructs real independent-source unequal-effect fibers on an open legal region.
body.consumer: The asymptotic square-root frontier determines how the minimum data moment order scales with latent complexity.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(s=\ell+3\) be the number of source columns
\[
 p_0,p_1,\ldots,p_\ell,q_\beta,e_y.
\]
For order \(r\), arrange their symmetric powers as the \(N_r\times s\) matrix
\[
 V_r=\bigl[p_0^{\otimes r}\ \cdots\ p_\ell^{\otimes r}\ q_\beta^{\otimes r}\ e_y^{\otimes r}\bigr],
 \qquad N_r=\binom{r+2}{2}.
\]
The three underlying vectors \(p_0,q_\beta,e_y\) form an invertible triangular matrix, so their degree-\(r\) evaluations are independent.  Evaluations at affine points \((1,u,v)\) span the dual of the ternary degree-\(r\) form space: a form vanishing at all such points is identically zero.  Therefore, whenever \(N_r\le s\), the remaining affine points can be chosen so that \(V_r\) has row rank \(N_r\).  Each chosen maximal minor is a nonzero polynomial.  Since \(N_r\le N_R\le s\) for \(2\le r\le R\), a generic choice makes all these minors nonzero simultaneously and also avoids every graph equality.

We next exhibit a full-dimensional legal source-moment chart.  Choose \(R+1\) distinct atoms admitting strictly positive centered weights.  The square Vandermonde matrix for moments of orders zero through \(R\) is invertible.  Restricting total mass to one and the first moment to zero gives a local affine isomorphism from the remaining \(R-1\) weights to \((m_2,\ldots,m_R)\).  Strict positivity is open, and the centered moment-to-cumulant transformation satisfies
\[
 \kappa_r=m_r+P_r(m_2,\ldots,m_{r-1}),
\]
so its Jacobian is triangular with diagonal one.  Thus each source admits an open chart in \((\kappa_2,\ldots,\kappa_R)\).  Every law in the chart has positive variance, finite support, and hence is non-Gaussian; taking their product enforces mutual independence.

Fix a parameter point in the intersection of this moment chart and the preceding loading-minor locus.  At each order \(r\), choose \(N_r\) columns forming an invertible matrix \(W_r\).  Vary the effect as \(\beta(t)=\beta+t\), hold \(\gamma,u_i,v_i\) fixed, and hold the unselected source cumulants fixed.  The graph coefficients become
\[
 b_i(t)=u_i-\gamma,\qquad c_i(t)=v_i-(\beta+t)u_i,
\]
and remain nonzero for all sufficiently small \(t\).  Solve the selected cumulants by
\[
 \kappa^{\mathrm{sel}}_r(t)
 =W_r(t)^{-1}\left\{C_r-\sum_{j\notin\mathrm{sel}}
 \kappa_{j,r}p_j(t)^{\otimes r}\right\},
 \qquad 2\le r\le R.
\]
All divisions are valid near zero because the selected determinants are nonzero.  The solution is rational and continuous in \(t\), equals the original source-cumulant vector at zero, and by construction keeps every complete tensor \(C_r\) fixed.  Openness of the finite-support moment charts supplies legal centered independent finite-support source laws for all sufficiently small \(t\).  Hence this is a curve in the common legal fiber and \(\beta(t)=\beta+t\) varies on it.

Let \(\mathcal V\) denote the parameter locus on which the chosen loading minors, moment-chart inequalities, and graph factors have the stated signs.  Derivatives of \(\Phi_{\ell,R}\) with respect to the selected source cumulants form the block diagonal matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(W_2,\ldots,W_R)\), so \(D\Phi_{\ell,R}\) is onto throughout \(\mathcal V\).  The preceding explicit inverses show directly that \(\Phi_{\ell,R}(\mathcal V)\) is Euclidean open: near any point, fix the structural coordinates and solve the selected cumulants for arbitrary nearby tensors.  This image is nonempty, consists of legal finite-support images, and every one of its fibers contains the constructed varying-effect curve.  Because it is open in the ambient cumulant space, it is Zariski dense; in particular it is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\).

It remains to deduce the frontier bounds.  Covariance nonidentification holds for every \(\ell\ge1\): use the one-latent covariance construction in the proof of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:one\mbox{-}latent\mbox{-}depth}\), and hold the normalized covariance contributions of the additional latent sources fixed.  Their graph factors stay nonzero on a sufficiently small effect interval.  Thus \(r_\beta(\ell)\ge3\).  If \(R\) is below the least integer satisfying \(\binom{R+2}{2}>\ell+3\), the result just proved rules out generic identification.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:depth}\) and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:strict\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}recovery}\) consequently give
\[
 L_\ell\le r_\beta(\ell)\le U_\ell.
\]
The defining quadratic inequalities imply
\[
 d_\ell=\sqrt{2\ell}+O(1),
 \qquad
 L_\ell=\sqrt{2\ell}+O(1),
\]
whereas \(\binom{h+3}{3}\ge\ell+1\) gives \(h_\ell=O(\ell^{1/3})\).  Hence
\[
 U_\ell=\sqrt{2\ell}+O(\ell^{1/3}).
\]
Dividing the two-sided bound by \(\sqrt{2\ell}\) and applying the squeeze argument proves \(r_\beta(\ell)/\sqrt{2\ell}\to1\).
